mechanisms: A neighbour's frame finishing takes a builder off its own (U9, 823 metal, three advanced solars: 0:armadvsol_28728 322, 5:armadvsol_15472 284, 6:armadvsol_14766 217): the hands' UnitFinished handler promotes the queued step of every builder whose started build is of the finished type within 250 of it, so when one of two adjacent advanced solars finished, the other builder's queued step began (a guard at once, or an armmakr that the blocked-site watchdog stopped 8 s later) and its frame was left at 62-92%; matching the finished unit to the builder's own frame (the id its UnitCreated gave) would have kept all three.

The exit-lane line answered with a leading 'stop' (U3, 704 metal, seven frames: 4:armnanotc_12832 168, 3:armsolar_15818 150, 5:armsolar_16263 135, 2:armadvsol_5052 130, 1:armsolar_20449 74, 4:armpb_21494 27, 4:armwin_144 20): a builder working from its plant's exit lane was reported as blocking it and the player re-listed it with 'stop' first; the stop landed 4-18 s after the report the player read, on frames that had grown meanwhile (11% to 97%, 30% to 87%, 56% to 73%); a rule that lets such a frame finish and then steps the builder out of the lane (or a stop that spares a frame past half) would have kept them.

One undefended home raid (U4, 780 metal, six frames over three seats: 7:armadvsol_30083 241, 7:armmoho_27594 155, 4:armmoho_2146 149, 0:armadvsol_20555 126, 0:armmoho_16900 99, 7:armrl_16876 10): party_645 (1 corak, 2 corpyro Fiends, tier 2) walked the north home row from A1 at 21:47 to D1 at 22:42 while every seat's army held the front; each seat's report carried it on the builder ('we cannot hit it ... it outclasses us: tier 2 against our tier 1') and the builders kept building; a home picket that can shoot tier-2 raiders (the players' or the commander's call) would have kept them.
